facts.text: GRaND Gamma-Ray Detector was deployed at Occator Crater (Cerealia Facula) during Dawn at Ceres in 2015.

Gamma Ray and Neutron Detector mounted on Dawn. Measured elemental concentrations of hydrogen, iron, potassium, and carbon by analyzing cosmic-ray-induced gamma emissions from the top meter of regolith.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the deep-space environment.
Discovered that water ice makes up roughly 10% to 30% of Ceres' upper regolith by weight, proving Ceres is a giant ice-rock world rather than a dead dry asteroid.
Status: Silent and dormant in deep space.
A permanent human and robotic monument celebrating space exploration in deep space.
